Market estimate: AAA's 81.8 million Thanksgiving travelers (Tue–Mon, 2025; the 2026 forecast comes out in mid-November) × metro New Orleans's 0.37% of the U.S. population × about half staying with family or friends × about 2½ nights = about 54,000 a day in the metro over the week (more on Thanksgiving and the two days after); about 1 in 15 visit the Quarter on a given day and 1 in 5 of those pass through the sheds (an estimate to check against vendor check-ins; smaller than the Christmas holidays, as Thanksgiving trips are shorter).

events.title: Locals and regional visitors
events.location: Residents of the metro area and day-trippers from the region
events.notes: Crowd: metro residents and regional day-trippers; families with kids on weekends and school holidays. About 370 today: a plain weekday. Many locals and regional visitors have been to the market many times, so depending on the merchandise, they may be less likely to buy than tourists, for whom everything is new and who are shopping for gifts and souvenirs. Market estimate: about a quarter of the market's visitors over a year are locals and regional visitors; this listing counts those not already in an event listing.

events.title: Sports: Bayou Classic visitors in town
events.notes: About 19 expected through the sheds from this listing today. • Bayou Classic visitors in town: about 750 of the weekend's overnight visitors (a quarter of the city calendar's 50,000 for the weekend count as staying downtown: many fans drive in for the day, and students and families on a budget stay in cheaper hotels farther out or with family) are in town and free the morning after the game; most drive home today, so half the usual rate (a travel day). Crowd: Southern and Grambling alumni, students and families, many of them college students and young adults. Market estimate: the weekend's own events and pop-ups around the Superdome and in the CBD (Fan Fest at Champions Square, the warm-up before the Battle of the Bands, the business showcase, the parade's CBD loop) pull visitors to that side of Canal St., so half the usual free-day rate, 1 in 20 × ½: about 19.
